def: A short document in which the delivery team writes down what it has understood, with assumptions and open questions marked, for the customer to correct and sign.
A number that can be computed from stated data, with a threshold, a baseline and an owner, that both sides agree decides whether the system worked.
The measured performance of the current process, computed the same way as the new system's metric, so that improvement can be judged.
A range of values that would contain the true rate in most repetitions of the same measurement, used to state how certain a measured metric is.
The chosen decision threshold on a model's scores, which sets how many true cases are caught and how many false alarms are raised.
A limit a project must stay inside, such as where data may go or which models are approved, that is met or broken rather than traded against other goals.
Conditions agreed in advance under which a project is stopped, such as a cost per task above a stated figure or a serious error in a regulated process.
A short note of a choice that shapes the work, giving the context, options, the decision, who made it and when to revisit it.
A technique in which the team imagines the project has failed and writes down the reasons, to surface risks and unstated assumptions early.
A second measure agreed alongside a target, such as review queue length beside recall, that catches the target being met in a harmful way.
